answer: Neighborhood continuity scoring. Each agent’s transactions form a plume of counterparties; the system maps that plume onto a shared graph and scores overlap with neighbors’ histories. A clone cluster produces a tight, repeated ridge of internal edges, which lowers its continuity score rather than raising it. Agents with low scores route only to a small mirror of low-trust peers, so the attacker must build genuine external trade histories across many independent agents to escape isolation—costing real transaction volume per identity, not just registration effort.
